content:
Apple today launched a new round of beta testing, and this time it came as quite a surprise: instead of rolling out the iPadOS 27.1 update as expected, the company jumped straight to iPadOS 27.2 beta 1.

Apple released iPadOS 27.2 beta 1 for testing, skipping iPadOS 27.1.

iPadOS 27 officially rolled out to all users this week, and Apple skipped 27.1 entirely, bringing developers iPadOS 27.2 beta 1.

It's still unclear why today's update wasn't a 27.1 build. The only thing we've heard about iOS 27.1 so far is that it will launch alongside the iPhone Duo.

Perhaps Apple plans to reserve 27.1 exclusively for iPhone Duo-related changes? Either way, we're looking forward to seeing what new features iPadOS 27.2 brings.

Before iPadOS 27 officially launched, Apple removed the Suggestions feature (previously available in Messages) as well as the option in the Passwords app that let users automatically replace compromised credentials with brand new secure ones through an agent-based approach.

Apple hasn't said when these features will return, but today's beta build could potentially bring them back.

Another possibility is a redesigned Health app, which Apple says will arrive later this year with new AI-powered enhancements.

Have you installed iPadOS 27.2 beta 1? Drop a comment and let us know about any new features you've discovered.
